item.title: In Minnesota, US cardinals and pope’s ambassador decry mass deportations and call for reconciliation
item.description: The prelates spoke of praying for everyone who has been affected — from the families of those killed to migrants and those assisting them to “the ICE men and women, too.”

item.title: Bishops to launch initiatives against violence on Ecuador-Colombia border
item.description: The Church in both countries is expressing concern about the impact of ongoing violence on local residents and stepping up joint efforts to provide pastoral accompaniment.

item.title: Vatican removes salty white film coating Michelangelo’s ‘The Last Judgment’
item.description: The Vatican on Saturday gave the media a sneak peak to the cleaning operation, which is taking place on a floor-to-ceiling scaffolding that has obscured the imposing fresco of heaven and hell that dominates the front of the chapel.

item.title: Pope warns against ‘spiral of violence’ as US attacks Iran
item.description: Pope Leo XVI, the world’s leading advocate for peace, urged an end to fresh violence in the Middle East following a series of missile strikes on Iran led by the United States and Israel.

item.title: Church should take a ‘critical and prophetic stance’ towards polarizing rhetoric, says Spanish archbishop
item.description: In an exclusive interview with Crux Now, Archbishop Joan Planellas of Tarragona said Christian values are “rooted in fraternity, social justice, and respect for human rights.”

item.title: Brazilian priest convicted of embezzling nearly 700 smart devices donated to his institute
item.description: A court found that Father Egídio de Carvalho Neto misappropriated 676 smartphones and tablets donated by the Federal Revenue Service when he was president of Instituto São José (Saint Joseph Institute).

item.title: Cardinal says priest who sent favorable letters to U.S. judge about El Mencho’s children ‘messed up’
item.description: The letters, disclosed last week by journalist Laura Sánchez Ley, were sent to Judge Beryl A. Howell of the District of Columbia in 2021 and 2025.

item.title: Conservative Anglican leaders meet in Nigeria, facing debate on a possible breakaway
item.description: The outlook for the Anglican Communion, one of the world’s largest families of Christian churches, remains uncertain, but some answers may emerge by the end of this week.

item.title: Pope Leo XIV renews calls for peace, dialogue as Iran strikes continue
item.description: The pope called for people everywhere “to truly strive to promote dialogue” and “seek solutions – to resolve problems without weapons.”
